title: CV
text:
Selected research and project experience

Vienna Waste Resilience
Independent spatial analysis · 2026

Developed a PostgreSQL/PostGIS workflow for analysing public waste collection infrastructure.
Constructed a 250 m analytical grid and calculated spatial redundancy and second-nearest-site accessibility.
Designed a simulated collection-site failure scenario.
Produced publication-ready thematic maps and documented methodological limitations.



Residential Locations and Everyday Accessibility in San Luis Obispo
Master’s thesis research · ongoing

Developing a GIS-based analysis of access to everyday infrastructure.
Combining accessibility measures with demographic, land-use and planning data.
Examining spatial patterns in the context of socially sustainable urban development.



Housing in the City Region of Lienz
Applied research project · 2025

Analysed the regional housing supply.
Contributed to surveys and stakeholder workshops.
Collaborated with actors from public administration, education and regional development.
Prepared findings for planning-oriented communication.



Solar Site Suitability in the Waldviertel
Group GIS project · 2024

Contributed to a multi-criteria site suitability analysis for photovoltaic infrastructure.
Worked with terrain, land-use, accessibility and visibility criteria in ArcGIS Pro.
Participated in fieldwork and project documentation.

title: About
text:
I am a geographer and master’s student based in Vienna. I hold a BSc in Geography and currently study Geographies of Global Change and Sustainability Transformations as well as Cultural and Social Anthropology at the University of Vienna.
My academic and project work focuses on urban geography, spatial inequality, accessibility and socially sustainable development. I am particularly interested in connecting spatial data analysis with an understanding of how urban environments are experienced, governed and transformed.

title: About
text:
Research approach
I combine quantitative spatial analysis with qualitative and policy-oriented research. Depending on the research problem, my work draws on GIS, SQL/PostGIS, statistical analysis, document analysis and qualitative coding.
This combination allows me to examine both the measurable spatial distribution of infrastructure and the social or institutional processes behind these patterns.
